verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. Lean states the k = 0 case only. `profile_stocks_rate` (and its localized twin) gives one constant C with |p_N - p_0| ≤ C/n in sup norm on a set S for all n above a threshold; there is no statement of the paper's ‖p_N - p_0‖_k for k ≥ 1, and no declaration was found that carries η-derivatives of the stock difference. The structural content of (4.40) — that the stock bound comes from Lemma 4.4(ii)/(4.17) applied to the profile and moment differences — is present as `profile_stocks_from_history_bounds`, but again at order 0: it consumes ‖ΔF‖_0, ‖ΔU‖_0 and ‖Δm‖_1 (value and first η-derivative of each history row) where the paper's (4.17) asks for ‖Δ(U,E)‖_{k+1} + ‖Δm‖_{k+1}, so the constant structure C_k(A_{k+1} + D_{k+1}) is not reproduced — Lean produces an unnamed constant from compactness instead. The hypothesis 0 < (P n).f p in the conclusion plays the role of the paper's "N large enough that E_N ≥ ½ min E_0". Rated low, not medium: the paper's later uses of P_k on pp. 42-43 are at order 0 ((4.41) uses P_0; Step 4 uses ‖p_f - p_N‖_0), so the orders that are missing are not the ones the surrounding argument consumes.
